member.name: T:FarPoint.Win.Spread.DrawingSpace.SpreadNotesContainer.NoteElements
member.summary: Base class still hold the list of CellNote object. NoteElements just override some functiosn to synchronize an index dictionary which use [Row, Column] as key and CellNote's index as value. So, we can access directly to any CellNote by the following code: this[(int)this.indexTable[new NoteLocation(CellNote.Row, CellNote.Column)]] Of course, you must check whether the index is existed or not. Other functions (GetNote, Find, IndexOf, Contains) are also overridded to gain better performance.

In spread, we can combine any of flag in DateTimeGroupingType, but in excel the enum ST_DateTimeGrouping only cover a subset of combine. members.member:
The DefaultFilter implementation of the ICustomFilterItem interface. This class performs Excel-like filtering by hiding rows that do not meet the filter criteria. In addition, the DefaultFilter can filter by applying a filtered-in style or filtered-out style to each row based on whether the row item meets the filter criteria.
Represents the default filtering of rows based on specified criteria.

member.name: T:GrapeCity.Utilities.GcTrace
member.summary: An trace helper to make an unity and configurable trace layer for difference platform: 'winform', 'wpf', 'silverlight' and 'winrt'.

remarks.example:
For 'WinForm' or 'WPF', you can add follow xml into you app.config to enable trace output.
<configuration> <system.diagnostics> <switches> <!-- available value include: 0: Off 1: Error 2: Warning 3: Info 4: Verbose --> <add name="@" value="4" /> <!-- '@' mean default switch. --> <add name="yourCustomSwatchName" value="1" /> </switches> </system.diagnostics> </configuration>

For 'Silverlight', you can add follow params into you page that embedded the silverlight component.
<object id="slPlugin1" width="300" height="50" data="data:application/x-silverlight-2," type="application/x-silverlight-2" > <param name="initParams" value="gcTrace=@:4;yourCustomSwitchName:1"/> </object>
The trace information will be write ot explorer's console. (For IE and Chrome, you can press F12 to show it)

member.name: M:FarPoint.Win.Spread.Model.CellRangeCollectionHelper.Union(System.Collections.Generic.List{FarPoint.Win.Spread.Model.CellRange},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Unites all the cell ranges which are adjoined or intersected. This method uses the unionRowsFirst parameter. The method starts by joining the adjoining or intersected cellranges which have the same row and row count (or column and column count), then joining the adjoining or intersected cell ranges which have the same column and column count (or row and row count). All cell ranges that are inside other cell ranges are removed. The method loops until no cell range can be united.
member.param: Indicates whether to join cell ranges with the same row and row count or the same column and column count first
member.returns: true if there are cell ranges to be joined

member.name: M:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindow(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings)
member.summary: The AnimateWindow function enables you to produce special effects when showing or hiding windows. There are four types of animation: roll, slide, collapse or expand, and alpha-blended fade.
member.param: Handle to the window to animate. The calling thread must own this window.
Specifies how long it takes to play the animation, in milliseconds. Typically, an animation takes 200 milliseconds to play.

Specifies the type of animation. Note that, by default, these flags take effect when showing a window. To take effect when hiding a window, use AW_HIDE and a logical OR operator with the appropriate flags.
member.remarks:
When using slide or roll animation, you must specify the direction. It can be either AW_HOR_POSITIVE, AW_HOR_NEGATIVE, AW_VER_POSITIVE, or AW_VER_NEGATIVE.
You can combine AW_HOR_POSITIVE or AW_HOR_NEGATIVE with AW_VER_POSITIVE or AW_VER_NEGATIVE to animate a window diagonally.
The window procedures for the window and its child windows should handle any WM_PRINT or WM_PRINTCLIENT messages. Dialog boxes, controls, and common controls already handle WM_PRINTCLIENT. The default window procedure already handles WM_PRINT.
If a child window is displayed partially clipped, when it is animated it will have holes where it is clipped.
member.returns: If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero; otherwise, the return value is zero.

member.name: T:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings
member.summary: Specifies the type of animation for showing the window.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_HOR_POSITIVE
member.summary: Animates the window from left to right. This flag can be used with roll or slide animation.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_HOR_NEGATIVE
member.summary: Animates the window from right to left. This flag can be used with roll or slide animation.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_VER_POSITIVE
member.summary: Animates the window from top to bottom. This flag can be used with roll or slide animation.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_VER_NEGATIVE
member.summary: Animates the window from bottom to top. This flag can be used with roll or slide animation.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_CENTER
member.summary: Makes the window appear to collapse inward if AW_HIDE is used or expand outward if the AW_HIDE is not used.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_HIDE
member.summary: Hides the window. By default, the window is shown.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_ACTIVATE
member.summary: Activates the window.

member.summary: Uses slide animation. By default, roll animation is used.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.AnimateWindowSettings.AW_BLEND

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.CustomDrawReturnValues.CDRF_DODEFAULT
member.summary: The control will draw itself. It will not send additional NM_CUSTOMDRAW notifications for this paint cycle. This flag cannot be used with any other flag.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.CustomDrawReturnValues.CDRF_NEWFONT
member.summary: Your application specified a new font for the item; the control will use the new font.
member.remarks: Supported from Shell and Common Controls Versions 6.0.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.CustomDrawReturnValues.CDRF_SKIPDEFAULT
member.summary: Your application drew the item manually. The control will not draw the item. This occurs when dwDrawStage equals CDDS_ITEMPREPAINT.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.CustomDrawReturnValues.CDRF_NOTIFYPOSTPAINT
member.summary: The control will send an NM_CUSTOMDRAW notification when the painting cycle for the entire control is complete.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.CustomDrawReturnValues.CDRF_NOTIFYITEMDRAW
member.summary: The control will notify the parent of any item-specific drawing operations. It will send NM_CUSTOMDRAW notification messages before and after it draws items. This occurs when dwDrawStage equals CDDS_PREPAINT.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.CustomDrawReturnValues.CDRF_NOTIFYSUBITEMDRAW
member.summary: Your application will receive an NM_CUSTOMDRAW message with dwDrawStage set to CDDS_ITEMPREPAINT | CDDS_SUBITEM before each list-view subitem is drawn. You can then specify font and color for each subitem separately or return CDRF_DODEFAULT for default processing. This occurs when dwDrawStage equals CDDS_ITEMPREPAINT.
member.remarks: Supported from Shell and Common Controls Versions 4.71.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.CustomDrawReturnValues.CDRF_NOTIFYPOSTERASE
member.summary: The control will notify the parent after erasing an item. This occurs when dwDrawStage equals CDDS_PREPAINT.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.WNDCLASSEX.hbrBackground
member.summary: Handle to the class background brush. This member can be a handle to the physical brush to be used for painting the background, or it can be a color value. A color value must be one of the following standard system colors (the value 1 must be added to the chosen color). If a color value is given, you must convert it to one of defined HBRUSH types. The system automatically deletes class background brushes when the class is unregistered by using UnregisterClass. An application should not delete these brushes. When this member is NULL, an application must paint its own background whenever it is requested to paint in its client area. To determine whether the background must be painted, an application can either process the WM_ERASEBKGND message or test the fErase member of the PAINTSTRUCT structure filled by the BeginPaint function.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.WNDCLASSEX.lpszMenuName
member.summary: Pointer to a null-terminated character string that specifies the resource name of the class menu, as the name appears in the resource file. If you use an integer to identify the menu, use the MAKEINTRESOURCE macro. If this member is NULL, windows belonging to this class have no default menu.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.WNDCLASSEX.lpszClassName
member.summary: Pointer to a null-terminated string or is an atom. If this parameter is an atom, it must be a class atom created by a previous call to the RegisterClass or RegisterClassEx function. The atom must be in the low-order word of lpszClassName; the high-order word must be zero. If lpszClassName is a string, it specifies the window class name. The class name can be any name registered with RegisterClass or RegisterClassEx, or any of the predefined control-class names. The maximum length for lpszClassName is 256. If lpszClassName is greater than the maximum length, the RegisterClassEx function will fail.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.WNDCLASSEX.hIconSm
member.summary: Handle to a small icon that is associated with the window class. If this member is NULL, the system searches the icon resource specified by the hIcon member for an icon of the appropriate size to use as the small icon.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.TooltipDuration.TTDT_AUTOMATIC
member.summary: Set all three delay times to default proportions. The autopop time will be ten times the initial time and the reshow time will be one fifth the initial time. If this flag is set, use a positive value of iTime to specify the initial time, in milliseconds. Set iTime to a negative value to return all three delay times to their default values.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.TooltipDuration.TTDT_RESHOW
member.summary: Set the amount of time it takes for subsequent ToolTip windows to appear as the pointer moves from one tool to another. To return the reshow delay time to its default value, set iTime to -1.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.TooltipDuration.TTDT_AUTOPOP
member.summary: Set the amount of time a ToolTip window remains visible if the pointer is stationary within a tool's bounding rectangle. To return the autopop delay time to its default value, set iTime to -1.

member.name: F:FarPoint.Win.Spread.NativeMethods.TooltipDuration.TTDT_INITIAL
member.summary: Set the amount of time a pointer must remain stationary within a tool's bounding rectangle before the ToolTip window appears. To return the initial delay time to its default value, set iTime to -1.

member.name: T:FarPoint.Win.Spread.IntellisenseRichTextBox
member.summary: Represents a rich text box with a transparent background color.
member.remarks:
We have two problems with IntellisenseRichTextBox: (1) HyperlinkRichTextBox: RichTextBox in .NET 2.0 just supports directly hyperlink which show text as hyperlink. In order to show a text for hyperlink, we need to hack RichTextBox with CHARFORMAT2_STRUCT. However, it's the reason when the RichTextBox is re-drawn automatically, we will lost the CHARFORMAT. To solve this problem, we need to re-create intellisense expression when it's necessary. (2) Transparent RichTextBox: RichTextBox in .NET 2.0 also doesn't support transparent background. So, we change Extented Style of this control in CreateParams to support transparent background (WS_EX_TRANSPARENT). One more problem is when we re-draw the IntellisenseRichTextBox, the font will be more bold (in actually, i don't know why :( ). Forturnately, i found a solution for this problem. It conerns to WM_SHOWWINDOW message. When IntellisenseRichTextBox receive this message, we will re-set its font by send WM_SETFONT message. The problem will be solved.
In summary, IntellisenseRichTextBox has not a good design. It's because of MS derived it from an old version of RichTextBox control (version 2.0). In future, i think we can re-design this class by two following choices: - Using Windowless Edit control: it's the best because it can work with RichTextBox version 2.0 - Derive from higher version of RichTextBox (it will causes deployment in Windows version such as Windows 2000..). Of course, we will also solve some problems about compatible ability. See the following reference snippet code:
